title: Merge Sorted Array
statement: Merge two sorted arrays into one sorted array in-place.

mistakes.hint1: Think about comparing two elements at a time rather than dealing with whole arrays.
mistakes.hint2: Use double pointers to keep track of your current position in both arrays.
mistakes.hint3: If you simply consider one element each at a time from the two arrays, make a decision, and proceed, you will arrive at the optimal solution.
mistakes.hint4: Since the first array has extra space at the end, try starting your pointers from the *back*!

mistakes.hint1: Make sure you only decrease the pointer for the array from which you just took an element.
mistakes.hint2: Are you accidentally shifting both pointers when you only placed one element?
mistakes.hint3: Trace what happens if array1 has [2] and array2 has [1]. Which pointer moves?
mistakes.hint4: Only modify pointer `i` if you pick from array1, and `j` if you pick from array2.

mistakes.hint1: When should your loop stop? Make sure both pointers stay within their array bounds.
mistakes.hint2: If pointer `i` reaches 0 but pointer `j` still has elements, you need to keep going.
mistakes.hint3: If pointer `j` reaches 0, you can actually stop, because array1 is already sorted in place.
mistakes.hint4: Use `while (i >= 0 && j >= 0)` for the main loop, then add a second loop just for `j >= 0`.

mistakes.hint1: Check how your code handles the case where one or both arrays only have one element.
mistakes.hint2: Does it crash or throw an out-of-bounds error?
mistakes.hint3: Ensure your loop bounds don't require at least 2 elements to function.

mistakes.hint1: What if one or both arrays are completely empty from the beginning?
mistakes.hint2: If the first array is conceptually empty (m=0), your code must just copy the second array over.
mistakes.hint3: Does your code crash if it tries to read index 0 of an empty array?
mistakes.hint4: Check your starting conditions. If `m==0`, just dump array2 into array1.

mistakes.hint1: How does your logic handle it when the current element in array A is exactly the same as the current element in array B?
mistakes.hint2: Are you skipping duplicates when you shouldn't be?
mistakes.hint3: Both elements must be included in the final merged array.
mistakes.hint4: Use `>=` instead of `>` to safely pick one and decrement its respective pointer.

mistakes.hint1: Review how you are deciding which element to place next. Is your > or < sign pointing the right way?
mistakes.hint2: If you are starting from the back, you need to place the LARGEST element first.
mistakes.hint3: Are you picking the smallest element and putting it at the end?
